summary: Christoph Anderl specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna and his PhD at the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier. He became a permanent member at Ghent University around 2013.

Christoph Cüppers works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1983, completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from circa 1998 to 2013.

Christoph Emmrich works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels by 2004, held a post there in 2001, and is attested as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto in 2026.

Sinologist and linguist Christoph Harbsmeier studied at Merton College, Oxford, and Copenhagen. He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia (1973–1976) and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980, later holding advisory professorships at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal universities.

Christoph Kleine specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bukkyo and Marburg (PhD 1995, Habilitation 2001), he was a professor at the University of Munich (2004–2008) before taking a professorship at the University of Leipzig in 2008.

Christoph Theodosius Walther was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and the LSE, was a professor at Osmania University in 1945, and served as Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London from circa 1951 to 1976.

Christophe Jaffrelot specializes in Indology. He studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca, took posts at Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London circa 2012.

Indologist Christophe Vielle has held academic posts including professor of Sanskrit at KU Leuven (attested 2009), professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013), and associate member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Christopher Andreas Holmboe worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the Royal Frederick University and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval, he served as Reader (1822) and Professor of Oriental Languages (1828–1876) at the University of Oslo.
Christopher Byrne is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at McGill University, where his PhD supervisor was Grace S. Fong.
Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is attested as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at the University of New Mexico, later holding faculty posts in philosophy and religious studies at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington, where he earned his MA and PhD and joined the faculty circa 1980.

Christopher Ives specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was an assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound from circa 1987 to 1993 and served as professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, where he completed his PhD in 2018 under the supervision of James A. Benn.
Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple specializes in Indology and religious studies. He was a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions in 1982 and served as Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University.

Christopher L. Diamond works in the fields of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Heidi R. M. Pauwels from circa 2012 to 2018 and held a post at the Australian National University around 2019.
